name: Halifax / Stanfield International Airport
before:
Nova Scotia's main airport, at Goffs in the Halifax Regional Municipality, and eighth busiest in Canada with 4,140,484 passengers in 2025. It serves mainland Nova Scotia and reaches into the neighbouring Maritime provinces.

It is a focus city for Air Canada and Porter Airlines, and the operating base for Cougar Helicopters, Maritime Air Charter and PAL Airlines.

The terminal has been substantially rebuilt. More than 200 million dollars has gone in since the Halifax International Airport Authority took over management in 2000, including an international arrivals area three times larger than its predecessor that opened in August 2001, with space set aside on its upper level for United States border preclearance, and a new domestic arrivals hall in December 2002.

The original 1960 building had two observation decks projecting over the apron and contained Nova Scotia's first escalators.

The airport is named after Robert Stanfield, the seventeenth premier of Nova Scotia.
after:
Nova Scotia's main airport and the largest in Atlantic Canada, at Goffs in the Halifax Regional Municipality. It was eighth busiest in Canada in 2025, with more than 4 million passengers.

Air Canada, Porter Airlines and PAL Airlines fly from here, and Cougar Helicopters and Maritime Air Charter are based at the airport.

The Halifax International Airport Authority has run the airport since 2000. It is the only airport in Atlantic Canada with United States border preclearance, so a client flying to the States clears US border checks here.

Nova Scotia's first escalator was installed in the original 1960 terminal.

The airport is named after Robert Stanfield, a former premier of Nova Scotia.

Charlottetown is suppressed for 2023 to 2025; its last published year (2022) was 339,450.
